Ferroptosis-related endothelial protection by Danhong injection in cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury: network pharmacology and validation in endothelial cells.

This study used network pharmacology, molecular docking, and endothelial cell experiments to identify shared therapeutic targets of Danhong injection in cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury. The authors report that DHI protects endothelial cells through ferroptosis-related mechanisms common to both organs. The work is largely computational and in vitro, so the clinical relevance remains to be validated.

Efficient flavonoids from Helichrysum bracteatum and their multi-target antioxidant mechanisms.

The authors optimized extraction of flavonoids from Helichrysum bracteatum using response surface methodology, achieving a 16.0% yield with quercetin, kaempferol, and rutin as the main components. The extract showed strong radical-scavenging activity, and network analysis was used to explore the multi-target antioxidant mechanisms underlying these effects.

Membrane lipid-driven gating of TREK-1 channels: Revisiting anesthetic mechanisms beyond protein targets.

This review examines how membrane lipid composition and lipid-driven conformational dynamics gate TREK-1 potassium channels, arguing that anesthetic mechanisms extend beyond direct protein binding to include lipid-mediated effects. It synthesizes evidence positioning TREK-1 at the intersection of protein-centric and lipid-centric frameworks for understanding general anesthesia.

Naturallyoccurring phytosterols in lipid nanoparticles induce rigidity reshape and endosome retention to enhance intracellular mRNA processing.

This study shows that replacing cholesterol in mRNA lipid nanoparticles with naturally occurring phytosterols bearing C-24 alkyl substitutions increases membrane rigidity and alters intracellular trafficking, causing the particles to be retained in endosomes in a way that improves mRNA processing and transfection efficiency. The authors link these gains to structure-activity relationships between sterol chemistry, LNP mechanics, and interactions with intracellular transport proteins, offering a rational design handle for next-generation mRNA delivery systems.

Mechanisms of Hofmeister ion effects on protein properties and their applications in food protein processing: A review.

This review synthesizes the mechanisms by which Hofmeister-series ions (especially anions) modulate protein properties, dissecting contributions from water-structure regulation and direct ion-protein interactions. It then surveys applications in food protein processing, including extraction, gelation, emulsion stabilization, and structural modification. The authors argue that the Hofmeister effect is best understood as an integrated phenomenon rather than a single mechanism.

Large-scale analysis of AlphaFold structures reveals organism-specific physicochemical signatures.

The authors analyzed physicochemical properties across 373,779 high-confidence AlphaFold-predicted protein structures and found systematic, organism-specific variation that is strong enough to recover major features of the tree of life. Notably, this phylogenetic signal persisted even when restricting the analysis to eukaryotic proteins, suggesting that structural physicochemical signatures carry organism-level information beyond simple taxonomic composition.

Effect of amino acid substitutions on the structure and dynamics of human PRPP synthetase PRPS1.

This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how disease-linked amino acid substitutions affect the structure and dynamics of human PRPP synthetase (PRPS1), an enzyme required for nucleotide synthesis. The authors find small but measurable correlations between structural changes and kinetic properties, notably that mutant A190V shows reduced feedback inhibition by ADP and GDP, consistent with enzyme superactivity. Increased flexibility is also observed in mutant Q1.

GNG2-MRAS interaction regulates SHOC2-dependent RAF activation and MAPK signaling.

This study identifies GNG2, the gamma subunit of heterotrimeric G proteins, as a negative regulator of MAPK signaling that acts by interacting with MRAS and disrupting the SHOC2-MRAS-PP1Cα holophosphatase complex. By blocking this complex, GNG2 prevents RAF dephosphorylation and activation, thereby dampening MAPK pathway output. The work clarifies the molecular mechanism of GNG2's tumor-suppressive-like role and suggests a new node for therapeutic intervention in cancers and RASopathies driven by MAPK dysregulation.

Predictive RNA-Ligand Binding Free Energy Perturbation through Preparatory Simulations and Polarizable Force Fields.

This paper extends free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations—a standard computational method for predicting how tightly drug-like molecules bind to proteins—to RNA targets, which are harder to model due to their flexibility, complex electrostatics, and metal-dependent binding. The authors show that careful preparatory simulations combined with polarizable force fields can make RNA-ligand binding predictions tractable, addressing when more sophisticated physical models are actually needed.

Enhancing Enzyme pH Adaptation for Industrial Biocatalysis: From Sequence-Dependent Engineering to Sequence-Independent Stabilization.

This review surveys strategies for improving enzyme performance under non-native pH conditions, which is a common bottleneck in industrial biocatalysis. It distinguishes sequence-dependent engineering approaches—such as rational mutation of ionizable residues and directed evolution—from sequence-independent stabilization methods like immobilization and formulation additives. The paper aims to provide a framework for choosing among these strategies for applications in detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutics.
